q: Parking Lot 基础需求包含哪些能力？（多选）
q_en: Which capabilities belong in the base Parking Lot requirements? (Select all that apply.)
options: 支持 Motorcycle、Car、Large Vehicle 三类车
入场时自动分配兼容车位并发 ticket
出场时用 ticketId 校验、计费、释放车位
支付处理、摄像头、预约和 UI
why: 基础系统只覆盖入场分配、票据、出场计费和释放车位；支付、摄像头、预约在需求澄清阶段被明确划为范围外。
why_en: The base parking lot handles compatible spot assignment, ticket issuance, ticket-based exit, and fee calculation, while payment, cameras, and reservations stay out of scope.
options_en: Support three vehicle types: motorcycle, car, and large vehicle.
Automatically assign a compatible spot and issue a ticket on entry.
Validate the ticket ID, charge a fee, and free the spot on exit.
Payment processing, cameras, reservations, and UI.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在入场时生成的停车会话凭证，出场时用它校验和计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ticket is the record the system creates at entry to represent one active parking session.

optionExplanations: 车型分类决定车位匹配规则，是入场分配必须支持的三类车。
入场是核心流程起点，车位匹配和发票必须自动完成，不用等人工分配。
出场校验、计费、释放车位三件事同时发生，是维持车位库存准确的关键闭环。
这些是需求澄清阶段被排除的功能，纳入会让基础版本失焦，属于后续迭代范围。
optionExplanations_en: Vehicle classification drives spot matching, so all three types have to be supported from day one.
Entry is the core workflow, so spot assignment and ticket issuance must happen automatically without a human in the loop.
Exit needs validation, billing, and spot release to happen together to keep the spot inventory accurate.
These were explicitly ruled out during requirements clarification — folding them in would blow the scope of the base design.

scenario: 系统只需要知道车辆是 motorcycle、car 还是 large 来匹配车位，不追踪车主、车牌或车辆状态。
scenario_en: The lot only needs to know whether a vehicle is a motorcycle, car, or large vehicle to match a spot; it does not track owner, plate, or vehicle state.
q: Vehicle（车辆）在 Parking Lot 设计中应如何建模？
q_en: How should Vehicle be modeled in this Parking Lot design?
options: VehicleType enum，而不是 Vehicle 类
完整 Vehicle 类，含车牌、车主、保险字段
把 Vehicle 定义为 Ticket 的父类
把 Vehicle 定义为 ParkingSpot 的子类
why: 车辆是外部对象，系统不追踪它的状态，只需要一个分类标签匹配车位类型；建成类会引入系统不需要管理的状态。
why_en: Vehicle stays a type enum because the lot only needs the vehicle category for spot compatibility, not an entity with tracked state.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求加入车牌识别、黑名单、常客账户或车辆历史，Vehicle 才可能成为实体。
tradeoff: 轻量分类枚举 vs 承载状态的完整实体
options_en: A VehicleType enum instead of a Vehicle class.
A full Vehicle class with license plate, owner, and insurance fields.
Define Vehicle as a parent class of Ticket.
Define Vehicle as a subclass of ParkingSpot.

termDefinitions.meaning: 枚举类型，用一组预定义的常量表示分类，例如车辆类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An enum is a fixed set of named constant values used to represent a category, like a vehicle type.

optionExplanations: 车辆只是车位匹配用的分类标签，枚举足够表达，不需要建成有状态的类。
把车主、保险这些系统不追踪的字段塞进类，是把外部对象误当成需要持久化的实体。
把 Vehicle 设成 Ticket 的父类颠倒了包含关系——票据描述一次会话，不该被车辆继承。
车辆不是车位的特化，两者是完全不同的领域概念，继承关系在语义上不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Vehicle is only a classification label for matching spots, so a plain enum already carries what a class would.
Loading owner and insurance fields onto Vehicle mistakes an external object for a stateful entity the system needs to persist.
Making Vehicle a parent of Ticket inverts the relationship — a ticket describes one session, it shouldn't be inherited from a vehicle.
A vehicle is not a specialization of a spot; treating it as a ParkingSpot subclass doesn't hold up semantically.

q: 最终设计中的核心实体/分类有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core entities or classifications are in the final design? (Select all that apply.)
options: ParkingLot（编排者，管理索引与流程）
ParkingSpot（物理车位数据）
Ticket（停车会话记录）
Vehicle 完整类（车主、保险等状态）
why: ParkingLot 编排，ParkingSpot 存物理属性，Ticket 记会话；Vehicle 只是外部分类标签，没有被建成类。
why_en: The model centers on ParkingLot, ParkingSpot, and Ticket as classes, while Vehicle stays a classification label rather than a class.
options_en: ParkingLot: the orchestrator that manages indexes and the workflow.
ParkingSpot: physical spot data.
Ticket: the record of one parking session.
A full Vehicle class holding owner and insurance state.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class ParkingLot
  class ParkingSpot
  class Ticket
  ParkingLot --> ParkingSpot
  ParkingLot --> Ticket
  Ticket --> ParkingSpot : spotId

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多个对象、驱动主流程的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An orchestrator is the component that coordinates other objects and drives the main workflow.

optionExplanations: 编排者持有索引和主流程，是入场出场逻辑真正跑起来的地方。
只存物理属性和车位类型，是无状态的纯数据对象，不掺业务逻辑。
记录一次停车会话的关键字段，出场计费和释放车位都靠它。
车主、保险这类持久状态从未被系统追踪，建成完整类是过度设计。
optionExplanations_en: The orchestrator holds the indexes and drives the actual entry/exit workflow.
It's a stateless data holder for physical properties and spot type only, with no business logic mixed in.
It records the key fields of one parking session, which both fee calculation and spot release depend on.
Owner and insurance data were never something the system tracks, so building a full class here is over-engineering.

scenario: 车辆入场时 ticket 一生成，该 spot 就被分配，即使车还没物理开到车位。
scenario_en: Once a ticket is issued at entry, that spot is assigned even before the car physically reaches it.
q: 本设计选择如何表示 occupied（占用）状态？
q_en: How does this design represent occupied state?
options: ParkingSpot 自己保存 occupied boolean
ParkingLot 维护 occupiedSpotIds Set 索引
完全从 activeTickets 每次动态推导
Ticket 自己负责释放车位
why: 占用被视为系统管理的 assignment 关系而非车位固有属性，由 ParkingLot 维护索引；Set 是受控冗余，换来 O(1) 查找和清晰的加锁边界。
why_en: ParkingLot tracks occupancy as an assignment relationship through an occupiedSpotIds Set, trading small redundancy for O(1) lookups and a clean locking boundary.
whenOtherWins: 如果更强调物理车位状态，ParkingSpot.occupied 也可行；Amazon Locker 就用了实体持有物理占用状态的方案。
tradeoff: 受控冗余换 O(1) 查找和并发边界 vs 零冗余但重复计算
options_en: ParkingSpot stores its own occupied boolean.
ParkingLot maintains an occupiedSpotIds Set as an index.
Derive occupancy from activeTickets on every lookup.
The Ticket itself frees the spot.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只存储唯一元素、支持快速成员判断的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Set stores unique elements and supports a fast membership check.

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作耗时不随数据规模增长，例如 Set 的成员判断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1) means an operation's cost does not grow with the size of the input, like a Set membership check.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一份信息在多处保存，需要额外维护同步，换取查询速度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization keeps the same information in more than one place, trading extra sync work for faster reads.

optionExplanations: 车位自己存 boolean 更直观，但要跟 ticket 状态两处同步，容易出现两个真相不一致的风险。
把占用看成系统维护的分配关系，用 Set 索引换 O(1) 查找，还能把加锁范围收紧到一个集合。
彻底不冗余，但每次分配都要扫全部 tickets，规模变大或写多读多时代价会显现。
释放车位应该是编排者的职责；让 Ticket 反过来操作 Spot，会打破谁拥有谁的边界。
optionExplanations_en: A boolean on the spot itself feels direct, but it has to stay synced with ticket state, so the two sources can drift apart.
Occupancy is treated as an assignment relationship rather than an intrinsic spot property, so a maintained Set buys O(1) lookups and a tight locking boundary.
Deriving from tickets on every lookup removes redundancy entirely, but the cost shows up once ticket volume or read frequency grows.
Freeing a spot is the orchestrator's job; letting Ticket reach back into Spot blurs who owns what.

q: Parking Lot 和 Amazon Locker 在占用状态建模上的核心差异是什么？
q_en: What is the core difference between Parking Lot and Amazon Locker occupancy modeling?
options: 两者都把占用看作车辆/包裹的物理存在状态
Parking Lot 和 Locker 都用同一个 Set 在编排者里维护占用
两者占用状态都由 Ticket/Token 自己持有并释放
Parking Lot 占用=ticket 分配关系，Locker 占用=物理包裹存在
why: 车位被分配给 ticket 是关系状态，包裹是否在格口是物理状态；这个语义差异解释了两套系统不同的占用建模。
why_en: Parking occupancy is assignment-like since a ticket references a spot, while locker occupancy is physical package presence, which explains the different modeling choices.
tradeoff: 关系型占用（assignment） vs 物理型占用（presence）
options_en: Both systems treat occupancy as the physical presence of a vehicle or package.
Both parking lot and locker maintain occupancy with the same Set on the orchestrator.
In both systems the ticket or token itself holds and releases the state.
Parking lot occupancy is a ticket-assignment relationship; locker occupancy is physical package presence.

termDefinitions.meaning: Amazon Locker 里用来验证取件人身份的一次性凭证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the one-time credential Amazon Locker uses to verify who may open a compartment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个电影订票系统案例，这里用来类比座位预订的占用关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BookMyShow is a movie-ticket booking case used here to compare seat-reservation occupancy.

optionExplanations: 包裹确实是物理进出格口，但车位靠 ticket 分配来表达占用，两者的语义并不相同。
Parking Lot 和 Locker 各自维护自己的占用索引，并不是共享同一个 Set。
Ticket 和 Token 是凭证，真正持有和清理占用状态的是各自的编排者，不是凭证自己。
关系型占用和物理型占用是两套不同语义：车位跟着 ticket 走，格口跟着包裹是否还在里面走。
optionExplanations_en: A package really is physically inside the compartment, but a spot's occupancy comes from a ticket assignment — the two aren't the same kind of state.
Parking Lot and Locker each maintain their own occupancy index; they don't share one Set.
Tickets and tokens are credentials — the orchestrator on each side actually holds and clears occupancy, not the credential itself.
These are two different kinds of occupancy: a spot follows its ticket assignment, while a compartment follows whether the package is still physically inside.

scenario: 系统不维护 occupiedSpotIds 索引，而是每次入场都从 activeTickets 动态计算哪些 spot 被占用。
scenario_en: The system does not maintain an occupiedSpotIds index; each entry request derives occupied spots from activeTickets.
q: 完全从 activeTickets 推导 occupiedSpotIds 的优点和缺点是什么？
q_en: What are the pros and cons of deriving occupiedSpotIds entirely from activeTickets?
options: 推导后无法知道 ticket 对应哪个 spot
推导版本反而比维护 Set 的写法运行起来更快，且完全没有任何额外代价
推导会自动避免所有并发 race
最少冗余，但每次分配要扫描 tickets，且并发时要锁整个 map
why: 推导状态概念上干净、没有冗余，但每次分配都要重复扫描 tickets，并发时还要锁住整个 activeTickets map；维护 Set 是受控冗余，换来清晰边界。
why_en: Deriving occupancy avoids redundancy but repeats the scan on every allocation and forces locking the whole ticket map under concurrency.
tradeoff: 零冗余的动态推导 vs 受控冗余的维护索引
options_en: Deriving occupancy makes it impossible to know which spot a ticket maps to.
The derived version is strictly faster than a maintained Set and carries no downside at all, in theory.
Deriving occupancy automatically prevents all race conditions.
It has the least redundancy, but allocation must scan tickets and concurrent access needs to lock the whole map.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多线程同时读写共享状态，导致结果依赖执行顺序的错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition happens when concurrent threads read and write shared state and the outcome depends on timing.

optionExplanations: ticket 本身还留着 spotId 字段，推导 occupied 集合并不会丢失这层映射。
扫描代替索引通常更慢不是更快，这个说法把工程代价说反了。
推导只是换了个读的方式，找空位和占用之间的 race 窗口照样存在。
没有额外索引要同步，但每次分配都要扫 tickets，并发下还得锁住整个 map，读写都变重。
optionExplanations_en: Ticket still stores its own spotId field, so deriving the occupied set doesn't lose that mapping.
Scanning in place of an index is typically slower, not faster — this claim has the tradeoff backwards.
Deriving just changes how you read state; the race window between finding and claiming a spot is still there.
There's no extra index to keep in sync, but every allocation scans tickets and concurrent access needs to lock the whole map, making both paths heavier.

q: 补全状态归属心法：
q_en: Fill in the state-ownership rule of thumb:
text: 判断状态属于实体还是 orchestrator，可问它是实体的{{内在属性}}，还是系统管理的{{关系/分配}}。
why: 车位大小是内在属性，当前被哪个 ticket 占用是关系状态；这个判断能解释很多 LLD 设计里的状态归属取舍。
why_en: State ownership depends on whether the state is intrinsic to an entity or a relationship the system manages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实体本身固有、不依赖外部关系的属性，比如车位的大小。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An intrinsic property belongs to the entity itself and does not depend on an external relationship, like a spot's size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由系统在多个对象之间维护的关系，比如车位当前分配给哪张 ticket。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relational state is a relationship the system maintains between objects, like which ticket a spot is currently assigned to.

scenario: 入场成功后，系统要在出场时识别停车会话、车位、车型和入场时间。
scenario_en: After entry succeeds, exit needs to identify the parking session, spot, vehicle type, and entry time.
q: Ticket 应保存哪些核心字段？
q_en: Which core fields should Ticket store?
options: id、spotId、vehicleType、entryTime
完整 ParkingSpot 引用、支付卡号、摄像头图片
只保存 vehicleType，其余现查
只保存 hourlyRate，不存时间
why: Ticket 是一次停车会话的不可变记录，出场计费和释放车位都依赖这四个字段，不多不少。
why_en: Ticket records the parking session with an ID, spot ID, vehicle type, and entry time, which is exactly what exit needs.
whenOtherWins: 如果要支持车牌识别或黑名单，需要新增专门实体，而不是把这些字段塞进 Ticket。
tradeoff: 只存最小必要字段 vs 塞进冗余引用和无关数据
options_en: id, spotId, vehicleType, and entryTime.
A full ParkingSpot reference, a payment card number, and a camera image.
Only vehicleType, looking everything else up later.
Only hourlyRate, without any timestamp.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class Ticket
  class Vehicle
  class ParkingSpot
  Ticket --> Vehicle
  Ticket --> ParkingSpot
  Ticket : spotId
  Ticket : entryTime

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接持有另一个对象的指针，可以调用它的方法或修改它的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An object reference directly points to another object, letting you call its methods or change its state.

optionExplanations: 这四个字段刚好覆盖出场要做的事：认票、找车位、算车型费率、算时长，不多不少。
支付卡号和摄像头图片跟停车会话记录无关，把它们塞进 Ticket 会让职责边界模糊。
丢了 spotId 和 entryTime，出场时无法知道该放哪个车位、该收多少钱。
没有 entryTime 就算不出停了多久，只存费率没法完成计费。
optionExplanations_en: These four fields cover exactly what exit needs: identify the ticket, locate the spot, know the rate, and compute duration — nothing extra.
A card number and camera image have nothing to do with the parking session record; folding them in blurs what Ticket is responsible for.
Without spotId and entryTime, exit has no way to know which spot to release or how long the car was parked.
Without an entry timestamp there's no way to compute duration, so storing only a rate can't produce a fee.

scenario: Ticket 需要在出场时告诉 ParkingLot 释放哪个车位，但不应该直接操作 ParkingSpot 对象。
scenario_en: Ticket must tell ParkingLot which spot to release at exit, but it should not mutate the ParkingSpot object directly.
q: Ticket 为什么存 spotId 字符串，而不是 ParkingSpot 对象引用？
q_en: Why should Ticket store a spotId string instead of a ParkingSpot object reference?
options: ParkingSpot 这个类本身完全不允许拥有一个 id 字段
Ticket 是记录，存 ID 更简单，避免它导航或修改 Spot
spotId 字符串无法用来释放车位
Ticket 必须自己负责定价计算
why: Ticket 不应该伸手修改领域对象。ParkingLot 用 spotId 更新 occupiedSpotIds 即可，符合 Law of Demeter。
why_en: Ticket stores a spot ID to remain a simple record rather than a navigational object that reaches into ParkingSpot.
tradeoff: 存 ID 的简单记录 vs 存对象引用带来的导航能力
options_en: ParkingSpot as a class is not allowed to have an id field at all.
Ticket is a record, and storing an ID is simpler and keeps it from navigating into or mutating Spot.
A spotId string cannot be used to free the spot.
Ticket must own the fee-calculation logic itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象只应该跟直接协作者通信，不应该链式访问别的对象内部结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says an object should only talk to its immediate collaborators, not reach through them into other objects.

optionExplanations: ParkingSpot 完全可以有自己的 id 字段，这个说法本身站不住脚。
Ticket 只是记录一次会话的事实，存字符串 ID 就够用，还能防止它反过来伸手修改 Spot 对象。
ParkingLot 拿到 spotId 就能在自己的索引里定位并释放对应车位，字符串完全够用。
计费是 ParkingLot 的职责，跟 Ticket 该存 ID 还是引用没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: ParkingSpot can absolutely have its own id field — this claim doesn't hold up.
Ticket only needs to record the facts of a session, so a string ID is enough, and it keeps Ticket from reaching back in to mutate Spot.
ParkingLot can look up and release the right spot from just the ID in its own index — a string is all it needs.
Fee calculation belongs to ParkingLot; it has nothing to do with whether Ticket stores an ID or a reference.

scenario: 需求只有一条定价规则：所有车型同一 hourly rate，按小时向上取整。
scenario_en: The only pricing rule is one hourly rate for all vehicle types, rounded up to whole hours.
q: 计费逻辑应放在哪个类里？
q_en: Which class should own the fee-calculation logic?
options: Ticket.calculateFee，并让 Ticket 自己保存 rate
ParkingLot.computeFee
ParkingSpot.getSpotType 顺带算价
VehicleType enum 内部计算
why: 计费是停车场业务政策，不是 ticket 记录本身的职责；简单需求下放在 ParkingLot 足够，也符合单一职责。
why_en: Fee calculation is a parking lot business policy, not behavior of the ticket record, so it belongs on ParkingLot.
whenOtherWins: 如果要支持多种复杂定价模型，可抽 PricingStrategy，而不是一开始就过度设计。
tradeoff: 定价放在业务编排者 vs 定价放在数据记录里
options_en: Ticket.calculateFee, with the ticket storing its own rate.
ParkingLot.computeFee.
ParkingSpot.getSpotType, computing price on the side.
Inside the VehicleType enum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类应该只有一个改变的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Single Responsibility Principle says a class should have only one reason to change.

optionExplanations: 让 Ticket 自己存费率会让一条会话记录背上业务政策，改价格时还要改每张已发 ticket 的逻辑。
计费是停车场的业务政策，不是某条记录或某个车位的职责，放在编排者身上最直接，也符合单一职责。
getSpotType 只该回答车位类型是什么，顺带算价会让一个方法承担两件不相关的事。
enum 只是分类值的集合，让它内部计算费用会把数据类型和业务逻辑混在一起。
optionExplanations_en: Having Ticket store its own rate saddles a session record with business policy, so a price change means touching every ticket's logic.
Fee calculation is a business policy of the lot, not the job of a single record or spot, so it fits naturally on the orchestrator and keeps a single responsibility.
getSpotType should only answer what type a spot is; tacking on pricing makes one method do two unrelated things.
An enum is just a set of classification values; making it compute fees mixes a data type with business logic.

scenario: 系统要把 $5.47 这样的金额存成整数，并按小时向上取整计费。
scenario_en: The system stores amounts like $5.47 as integers and bills parking time by rounding up to whole hours.
q: 补全计费锚点：
q_en: Fill in the billing anchor:
text: 金额应以最小货币单位如 {{cents}} 的整数保存；时长按小时计费并 {{向上取整}}，所以 5 分钟也算 1 小时。
why: 金额用 cents 整数存储避免浮点误差（$5.47→547 cents）；时长向上取整这条规则直接决定 computeFee 的返回值。
why_en: Money is stored as integer cents to avoid floating-point error, and duration rounds up to whole hours, which directly drives computeFee's output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用整数分表示金额，避免浮点小数误差累积。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Storing money as integer cents avoids the rounding errors that accumulate with floating-point fractions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不足一个整小时也按一整小时计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rounding up means any partial hour is still billed as a full hour.

scenario: 出场 API 收到 ticketId，需要快速验证票据并找到 entryTime 和 spotId。
scenario_en: The exit API receives a ticketId and must quickly validate the ticket and find entryTime and spotId.
q: activeTickets 应该用什么结构存储？
q_en: What data structure should store activeTickets?
options: List<Ticket>，每次都要做一遍线性扫描，是唯一能用的选择
Map<String, Ticket>，以 ticketId 为 key
Set<ParkingSpot>，按车位去重
单个 currentTicket 字段
why: map 让『按 ticketId 查票』的意图显式化；200 张票时 benchmark 显示 map 0.12μs、list 扫描 1.93μs，但这个差距在停车场规模下不重要，map 的价值主要在代码可读性。
why_en: A map makes lookup-by-ticket-ID explicit, and even though it benchmarks faster than a list scan, the real win at parking-lot scale is code clarity.
whenOtherWins: 极小系统用 list 扫描也能工作，但没有 map 语义清楚。
tradeoff: 查找语义清晰的 Map vs 实现简单但要线性扫描的 List
options_en: List<Ticket>, where a full linear scan every time is the only option available.
Map<String, Ticket>, keyed by ticket ID.
Set<ParkingSpot>, deduplicated by spot.
A single currentTicket field.

termDefinitions.meaning: 键值对集合，可以通过 key 直接查找 value。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Map stores key-value pairs and lets you look up a value directly by its key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作耗时不随数据规模增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1) means an operation's cost does not grow with the size of the input.

optionExplanations: 线性扫描能跑通，但用循环代替按键查找，会把查询逻辑藏起来，可读性不如直接查表。
用 ticketId 做 key，查找意图一目了然，还顺带拿到近乎 O(1) 的性能，规模变大后差距更明显。
这里要按 ticketId 找票据，不是按车位去重，Set<ParkingSpot> 从数据结构上就答非所问。
系统同时有多张有效票据在场，单个字段连基本的多会话场景都装不下。
optionExplanations_en: A linear scan can work, but looping instead of keying by ID buries the lookup logic, which reads worse than a direct lookup.
Keying by ticketId makes the lookup intent obvious and happens to run near O(1), and that gap only widens as ticket volume grows.
The job here is finding a ticket by ID, not deduplicating spots, so a Set<ParkingSpot> answers a different question entirely.
Multiple sessions are active at once, so a single field can't even represent the basic case of more than one ticket.

scenario: 车辆入场，系统要找兼容空位并发票。
scenario_en: A vehicle enters, and the system must find a compatible free spot and issue a ticket.
q: 这段 enter 伪代码体现的状态变化顺序是什么？
q_en: What state-change order does this enter pseudocode show?
codeSample:
enter(vehicleType)
    spot = findAvailableSpot(vehicleType)
    if spot == null throw NoSpace
    occupiedSpotIds.add(spot.id)
    ticket = Ticket(generateId(), spot.id, vehicleType, now())
    activeTickets[ticket.id] = ticket
    return ticket
options: 先创建 ticket，稍后再决定占不占车位
只更新 ParkingSpot.occupied，不碰 ticket
先占用 spotId，再创建并保存 ticket，最后返回 ticket
把车位分配推迟到出场时才做
why: 入场成功要同时建立车位占用索引和票据索引；找不到兼容空位时不能改变任何状态。
why_en: Entry claims a compatible spot, creates a ticket, stores it, and returns it, keeping both indexes in sync.
whenOtherWins: 多入口并发下，这段 find+add 必须放在同一把锁内，否则两辆车可能拿到同一个车位。
tradeoff: 先占位后发票保证不变量 vs 反过来可能留下幽灵占用
options_en: Create the ticket first and decide whether to claim a spot later.
Only update ParkingSpot.occupied, without touching the ticket.
Claim the spot ID first, then create and store the ticket, then return it.
Defer spot assignment until exit time.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["vehicle arrives"] --> B["find spot"]
  B --> C["mark spot occupied"]
  C --> D["create ticket"]
  D --> E["store active ticket"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在任何时刻都必须保持成立的约束，例如 occupied 集合和 ticket 集合同步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a condition the system must always keep true, such as keeping the occupied set and ticket map in sync.

optionExplanations: 先发票据再决定占位，会让系统一度出现有效 ticket 却没对应车位的中间态。
只改 occupied 不建票据，出场时就没有 ticket 可查，出场流程直接断裂。
占位、建票、存票、返回，四步顺序保证两个索引在任何时刻都同步，不会留下半成品状态。
入场就是要当场确定车位，推到出场才分配等于让 ticket 在整个停车期间都指不到具体车位。
optionExplanations_en: Issuing the ticket before deciding on a spot leaves a window where a valid ticket exists with no spot behind it.
Updating only occupied without creating a ticket means exit has nothing to look up, breaking the exit flow entirely.
Claim the spot, build the ticket, store it, then return it — that order keeps both indexes in sync with no half-finished state in between.
Entry is exactly when the spot has to be pinned down; deferring it to exit means the ticket points nowhere for the whole stay.

scenario: 基础需求要求 exact compatible spot，不提『摩托可停汽车位』等 fallback。
scenario_en: The base requirement asks for an exact compatible spot and does not mention fallback rules like letting motorcycles use car spots.
q: findAvailableSpot 默认应如何查找空位？
q_en: How should findAvailableSpot look for a free spot by default?
options: 扫描 spots，找 spotType 匹配且不在 occupiedSpotIds 中的空位
任意一个空位，都可以直接随便分配给任何车型，完全不检查 spotType 是否匹配
优先把停车场里最大的车位分配给所有车型，不管实际需要
按车辆到最近出口的实时距离做复杂路径排序后再分配
why: 基础规则是兼容类型精确匹配。没有需求提出 fallback 时不引入复杂分配策略。
why_en: The base allocation scans for an unoccupied spot with the required compatible type, nothing more.
whenOtherWins: 如果扩展允许 motorcycle 用 car spot，映射逻辑或分配策略需要支持 fallback 顺序。
tradeoff: 精确类型匹配的简单扫描 vs 提前引入的复杂分配策略
options_en: Scan spots for a matching spotType whose id is not in occupiedSpotIds.
Any single free spot at all can be handed to any vehicle type freely, without ever checking spotType.
Always give the largest spot in the lot to every vehicle type.
Sort candidate spots by real-time distance to the nearest exit.
optionExplanations: 基础规则就是类型精确匹配加空闲检查，两个条件缺一不可，逻辑最直接对应需求。
跳过类型检查会让摩托车占用汽车位这种情况随意发生，违反了『兼容车位』这个前提。
把大车位都给小车会白白浪费本该留给大车的稀缺资源，也不是需求要的规则。
需求根本没提出口距离或路径优化，提前引入这套排序是没有依据的复杂化。
optionExplanations_en: The base rule is exact type match plus a free check — both conditions map directly to what was actually asked for, nothing more.
Skipping the type check would let a motorcycle claim a car spot at will, which breaks the compatible-spot requirement.
Handing large spots to every vehicle wastes a resource that should stay reserved for large vehicles, and nothing in scope asked for that.
Nothing in the requirement mentions exit distance or path optimization, so adding that sorting logic now has no basis.

scenario: 用户出场提供 ticketId，ticket 存在且未使用过。
scenario_en: A user exits with a ticketId, and the ticket exists and has not been used before.
q: exit 的正确执行顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct execution order for exit?
options: 出场时先把 activeTickets 里对应的 ticket 直接删除掉，然后再用它去计算 fee
查 ticket → 计算 fee → 释放 spot → 删除 active ticket → 返回 fee
只计算 fee 返回给用户，不释放 spot，占用状态一直保留
把该车位所在楼层的所有同类型车位全部释放，而不是只放这一个
why: 出场完成后车位可再次分配，ticket 不能再次使用；顺序必须保证 ticket 数据还在时先完成计费。
why_en: Exit looks up the ticket, computes the fee, frees the spot, removes the active ticket, and returns the fee, in that order.
whenOtherWins: 如果计费失败需要重试，删除 ticket 这一步应该放到计费和释放都确认成功之后再做。
tradeoff: 先读数据再清理状态 vs 先清理导致计费数据丢失
options_en: Delete the matching ticket from activeTickets first, and only afterward try to use it to compute the fee.
Look up the ticket, compute the fee, free the spot, remove the active ticket, then return the fee.
Only compute the fee without freeing the spot, leaving occupancy untouched.
Free every same-type spot on that floor, not just this one.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant V as Vehicle
  participant L as ParkingLot
  participant T as Ticket
  V->>L: exit(ticketId)
  L->>T: load active ticket
  L->>L: calculate fee
  L->>L: free spot
  L->>L: remove active ticket
optionExplanations: 计费需要用到 ticket 里的 entryTime，先删掉它就等于把算 fee 需要的数据先扔了。
先读票再算钱，最后才清理两个索引，保证每一步都还能拿到上一步留下的数据。
不释放车位等于让这个车位在系统里永远显示占用，下一辆车永远排不上它。
出场只该影响这一个车位，把整层同类型全放掉会错误地清空别人正在用的车位。
optionExplanations_en: Fee calculation needs the entryTime stored on the ticket, so deleting it first throws away the data the fee math depends on.
Read the ticket, compute the fee, then only afterward clean up both indexes — each step still has the data the previous one needs.
Skipping the release leaves that spot permanently marked occupied, so no future car can ever be assigned to it.
Exit should only touch this one spot; freeing every same-type spot on the floor would wrongly clear spots other vehicles are still using.

scenario: 用户可能重复使用同一张 ticket 出场。
scenario_en: A user may try to exit more than once with the same ticket.
q: 这段 exit 伪代码如何防止 double exit？
q_en: How does this exit pseudocode prevent a double exit?
codeSample:
exit(ticketId)
    if ticketId == null || ticketId == '' throw InvalidTicket
    ticket = activeTickets[ticketId]
    if ticket == null throw InvalidTicket
    fee = computeFee(ticket.entryTime, now())
    occupiedSpotIds.remove(ticket.spotId)
    activeTickets.remove(ticketId)
    return fee
options: 在 Ticket 上增加 usedCount 字段计数
允许重复计费，只记录日志
成功出场后删除 activeTickets 项，下一次查不到同一 ticket
只删除 occupiedSpotIds 这一个索引，但仍然把 ticket 本身保留着
why: activeTickets 是当前有效票据集合，移除后已使用票据和随机无效票据都表现为同一种 invalid。
why_en: Removing the ticket from activeTickets makes any repeated exit with the same ticket ID come back invalid.
whenOtherWins: 如果要区分『从未存在』和『已使用』这两种错误，需要额外维护 usedTickets 或历史记录。
tradeoff: 用集合成员资格表达有效性 vs 额外状态字段表达已用
options_en: Add a usedCount field on the Ticket to count exits.
Allow repeated billing and only log it.
Remove the entry from activeTickets on success, so the next lookup finds nothing.
Only remove the occupiedSpotIds index entry, while still keeping the ticket itself around.
optionExplanations: 加计数字段能记录次数，但没有真正拒绝第二次出场，还得再加一层判断逻辑才有用。
记日志只是留证据，不能阻止用户被重复扣费，风险没有被真正堵住。
出场成功就把票从有效集合里摘掉，第二次查询天然查不到，问题在根上被消除。
留着 ticket 但删了占用记录，第二次出场还能查到同一张票，重复扣费的口子没堵上。
optionExplanations_en: A counter can log how many times exit ran, but it doesn't actually reject the second attempt — you'd still need extra logic on top.
Logging keeps a record but does nothing to stop the user from being billed twice; the actual risk stays open.
Once exit succeeds, the ticket disappears from the valid set, so a second lookup naturally finds nothing — the problem is removed at the source.
Keeping the ticket while only clearing occupancy still lets a second exit find the same ticket, so double billing stays possible.

scenario: 系统用 durationMillis 表示停车时长，按小时向上取整计费，hourlyRateCents=500。
scenario_en: The system represents parking duration as durationMillis, bills by rounding up to whole hours, and uses hourlyRateCents = 500.
q: computeFee 应该如何处理 2.5 小时这类不足整数小时的时长？
q_en: How should computeFee handle a partial-hour duration such as 2.5 hours?
options: 把算出来的小数 durationHours 四舍五入到最近整数小时
durationMillis 对 3600000 取模，余数 > 0 就 hours+1，再乘费率
忽略不足一小时的余量，只按整除后的小时数收费
直接用浮点数 durationMillis/3600000.0 去乘以小时费率来计算出结果
why: 需求是不足一小时也按一小时收费，只有『余数>0则hours+1』能保证任何非零余量都进位；四舍五入和向下取整都会算错 2.5 小时的场景。
why_en: The rule is that any partial hour still bills a full hour, so only the remainder-then-increment check gets a 2.5-hour stay right.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品要求首小时免费或按分钟计费，这段取整逻辑要整体替换。
tradeoff: 余数判断的整数取整 vs 四舍五入或浮点近似
options_en: Round the fractional durationHours to the nearest whole hour.
Take durationMillis modulo 3600000; if the remainder is greater than 0, add one hour before multiplying by the rate.
Ignore the partial-hour remainder and bill only the floored whole hours.
Directly multiply the raw floating-point durationMillis/3600000.0 by the hourly rate to compute the final result.
codeSample:
computeFee(entryMs, exitMs)
    durationMs = exitMs - entryMs
    hours = durationMs / 3600000
    if durationMs % 3600000 > 0
        hours = hours + 1
    return hours * hourlyRateCents

termDefinitions.meaning: 两数相除后的余数运算，用 % 表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo is the remainder operation after division, written with the % operator.

optionExplanations: 四舍五入会把 2.5 小时收成 2 小时，恰好违反了『不足一小时也要收一小时』这条规则。
只要余数不为零就进一位，这是唯一能保证任何非零零头都被收费的写法。
向下取整等于把不到一小时的零头当成免费送出，跟计费规则直接冲突。
浮点除法在边界值上可能因精度误差算错临界小时，整数取模不会有这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Rounding to nearest would bill 2.5 hours as 2, directly violating the rule that any partial hour still bills a full hour.
Bumping the hour count whenever the remainder is nonzero is the only version that guarantees every partial hour gets billed.
Flooring effectively gives the leftover partial hour away for free, which contradicts the billing rule outright.
Floating-point division can misjudge a boundary hour due to precision error near the edge; integer modulo avoids that entirely.

q: ParkingLot 应处理哪些基础错误？（多选）
q_en: Which base errors should ParkingLot handle? (Select all that apply.)
options: 无兼容空位时拒绝入场
ticketId 空或不存在时拒绝出场
已使用 ticket 再次出场时拒绝
金额用浮点数导致精度误差
why: 前三个是业务错误处理要求，最后一个是实现风险；金额用整数 cents 存储能避开浮点精度问题。
why_en: The design rejects full-lot entry, invalid or reused tickets, and uses integer money to avoid floating-point precision errors.
options_en: Reject entry when no compatible spot is available.
Reject exit when the ticket ID is empty or does not exist.
Reject exit when a used ticket is presented again.
Using floating-point money causes precision drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浮点数用二进制近似小数，反复运算会累积微小误差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Floating-point numbers approximate decimals in binary, so repeated arithmetic accumulates small errors.

optionExplanations: 车位满了还硬发票据会留下无法兑现的记录，入场必须在这一步就拦住。
空字符串或不存在的 ID 如果放行，出场逻辑会在查表那一步直接崩掉或返回垃圾数据。
重复出场如果不拦，同一张票能被反复计费和反复释放，账和车位都会乱。
浮点数做加减乘除会累积舍入误差，金额算错几分钱这种 bug 很难被单元测试抓到。
optionExplanations_en: Issuing a ticket when the lot is full would create a record with no spot behind it, so entry has to be blocked right here.
Letting an empty or nonexistent ID through would crash or return garbage at the lookup step in the exit flow.
If a used ticket isn't rejected, the same ticket could be billed and released more than once, corrupting both money and spot state.
Floating-point arithmetic accumulates rounding error, so a fee that's off by a few cents is exactly the kind of bug unit tests tend to miss.

scenario: VehicleType 和 SpotType 目前都只有 MOTORCYCLE/CAR/LARGE 三个值，取值完全相同。
scenario_en: VehicleType and SpotType currently both contain MOTORCYCLE, CAR, and LARGE, with identical values.
q: 为什么 VehicleType 和 SpotType 即使值相同也要分成两个 enum？
q_en: Why keep VehicleType and SpotType as separate enums even when their values match?
options: 车辆类型和车位类型是不同概念，未来兼容关系可能变化
编程语言不允许两个类复用同一组常量
只是为了增加类的数量，方便面试展示
因为 Ticket 类型上不能存 VehicleType 字段
why: 分开建模让『摩托可停汽车位』这类兼容逻辑更清晰；相同标签不代表两者是同一个领域概念。
why_en: Vehicle type and spot type are different concepts even though their current labels match, which keeps future compatibility rules clean.
tradeoff: 语义分离换未来兼容逻辑的清晰 vs 合并 enum 省一个类型定义
options_en: Vehicle type and spot type are different concepts, and their compatibility rules may diverge later.
The programming language forbids two classes from reusing the same constants.
It is only done to add more classes for the interview to look impressive.
Because Ticket cannot store a VehicleType field.
optionExplanations: 车辆类型和车位类型现在恰好同值，但一个描述车、一个描述车位，摩托停汽车位这类规则出现时会先分家。
任何主流语言都能让两个类型各自定义相同的常量集合，这条限制并不存在。
拆成两个 enum 是为了让兼容规则以后能独立演化，不是单纯凑类的数量。
Ticket 存 VehicleType 字段完全没问题，这跟要不要拆分 enum 没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Vehicle type and spot type happen to share the same values today, but one describes a car and the other a spot — once fallback rules like motorcycle-in-car-spot show up, they diverge first.
Any mainstream language lets two types define their own matching sets of constants; that restriction doesn't exist.
Splitting them into two enums is about letting compatibility rules evolve independently, not padding the class count.
Ticket storing a VehicleType field is completely fine and has nothing to do with whether the enums are split.

scenario: ParkingSpot 在当前设计中只表示物理车位的固有属性，不参与占用或计费逻辑。
scenario_en: In the current design, ParkingSpot only represents intrinsic physical spot properties and does not own occupancy or pricing logic.
q: ParkingSpot 需要哪些字段？
q_en: Which fields does ParkingSpot need?
options: occupied boolean、ticket map、hourlyRate
id 和 spotType
entryTime 和 fee
全部 activeTickets 的引用
why: ParkingSpot 是纯数据对象，只保存物理身份和兼容类型；占用和票据由 ParkingLot 管理。
why_en: ParkingSpot stores only intrinsic properties: its ID and spot type.
whenOtherWins: 如果选用实体自管物理占用的方案，可以在 ParkingSpot 上加 occupied/status 字段。
tradeoff: 只存内在属性的纯数据对象 vs 把关系状态也塞进实体
options_en: An occupied boolean, a ticket map, and an hourly rate.
id and spotType.
entryTime and fee.
A reference to every entry in activeTickets.
optionExplanations: occupied、ticket map、rate 都是关系或业务状态，ParkingSpot 只该管自己的物理属性。
身份和车位类型是车位真正内在、不依赖任何关系就存在的属性，其余都该由编排者管理。
entryTime 和 fee 属于某一次会话，是 Ticket 的字段，跟车位本身的固有属性无关。
让每个车位持有全部票据引用会造出严重冗余，而且车位根本不需要知道别的会话。
optionExplanations_en: occupied, a ticket map, and rate are all relationship or business state — ParkingSpot should only own its own physical properties.
Identity and spot type are the only things truly intrinsic to a spot, independent of any relationship; everything else belongs to the orchestrator.
entryTime and fee belong to a specific session, which is Ticket's job, not an intrinsic property of the spot itself.
Giving every spot a reference to all tickets creates massive redundancy, and a spot has no reason to know about sessions it isn't part of.

q: 按顺序排列一次停车会话的状态变化：
q_en: Put one parking session's state changes in order:
steps: findAvailableSpot 找到空车位 B。
occupiedSpotIds 加入 B。
创建 Ticket(T123,B,CAR,entryTime) 并放入 activeTickets。
exit(T123) 计算 fee。
occupiedSpotIds 删除 B，activeTickets 删除 T123。
why: 同一会话由 occupiedSpotIds 和 activeTickets 两个索引共同表达，出场必须同时清理两者。
why_en: A parking session claims a spot, stores a ticket, computes a fee on exit, and clears both indexes together.
tradeoff: 双索引同步表达一次会话 vs 单一来源每次动态推导
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Gate
  participant Lot
  participant Ticket
  Gate->>Lot: enter(CAR)
  Lot->>Lot: claim spot B
  Lot->>Ticket: create T123
  Gate->>Lot: exit(T123)
  Lot->>Lot: fee and release B

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了快速查找而额外维护的数据结构，需要和源数据保持同步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is extra data maintained purely to make lookups fast, and it must stay in sync with the source data.

scenario: Ticket 已经发给用户，后续会用来计费和释放车位。
scenario_en: The ticket has already been issued to the user and will later be used for billing and releasing the spot.
q: Ticket 字段应如何设计？
q_en: How should Ticket fields be designed?
options: 允许用户修改 entryTime
让 ParkingSpot 反过来修改 ticketId
构造后只读，不暴露任何修改方法
每次出场前随机重写 spotId
why: Ticket 是会话记录，应稳定反映入场事实；不可变让计费和验证更可靠，避免被意外篡改。
why_en: Ticket should be immutable because it records the facts of the parking session and must stay reliable for billing and validation.
whenOtherWins: 如果未来要支持改签停车时段，才需要给 Ticket 加受控的状态转换方法，而不是暴露 setter。
tradeoff: 不可变记录保证计费可靠 vs 可变字段带来的一致性风险
options_en: Allow the user to modify entryTime.
Let ParkingSpot modify the ticketId in return.
Read-only after construction, with no exposed mutation methods.
Randomly rewrite spotId before every exit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象创建后字段不能再被修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An immutable object cannot have its fields changed after it is created.

optionExplanations: entryTime 是入场那一刻的事实，允许改写就等于允许伪造停车时长，直接威胁计费的可靠性。
Ticket 的 spotId 应该是它记录的既成事实，反过来让 Spot 改写它会打破谁描述谁的方向。
创建后不可变，让票据能稳定反映入场事实，计费和出场验证都能放心信任它不会被中途篡改。
spotId 一旦写入就不该再变，随机重写会让票据跟真实占用的车位对不上。
optionExplanations_en: entryTime is the fact of the moment entry happened; letting it be edited is letting someone fake how long they parked, which undermines billing directly.
spotId on the ticket should be a fact the ticket records; letting Spot rewrite it backwards breaks the direction of who describes whom.
Being read-only after construction means the ticket reliably reflects the entry fact, so billing and exit validation can trust it wasn't tampered with mid-session.
Once spotId is written it shouldn't change again; randomly rewriting it would make the ticket point at the wrong spot.

scenario: 后续要求 motorcycle 3 美元/小时，car 5 美元/小时，large 8 美元/小时。
scenario_en: A later requirement sets different hourly rates: motorcycle $3, car $5, and large vehicle $8.
q: 最简单合理的扩展方式是什么？
q_en: What is the simplest reasonable extension?
options: 立刻抽出 PricingStrategy 接口，为单一规则做多态扩展
让 Ticket 自己保存三档价格并在内部计算费用
为每一种不同的 SpotType 都各自单独实例化出一整个 ParkingLot 系统出来处理
ParkingLot 存 Map<VehicleType,rate>，computeFee 按车型查表
why: 只有按车型不同费率这一条规则时，一个 map 就足够简单；Strategy 模式留给更复杂、可动态替换的定价规则。
why_en: A map from vehicle type to hourly rate is enough for simple per-type pricing, without introducing a strategy interface.
whenOtherWins: 如果要支持动态定价、折扣、会员或节假日策略，PricingStrategy 才更合适。
tradeoff: 按车型查表的简单扩展 vs 提前上 Strategy 模式的过度设计
options_en: Introduce a PricingStrategy interface right away for a single rule.
Let the Ticket store all three price tiers and compute its own fee.
Instantiate a whole separate ParkingLot system entirely on its own for every single distinct SpotType out there.
ParkingLot stores a Map<VehicleType, rate> and computeFee looks it up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 键值对集合，这里键是 VehicleType，值是对应费率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Map<K,V> stores key-value pairs — here the key is a vehicle type and the value is its hourly rate.

optionExplanations: 只是三档固定费率，还没出现『需要在运行时切换算法』这种情况，上接口是提前买单。
费率是停车场的业务政策，让每张票各存一份价格表，改价时要挨个改，维护成本更高。
车型不是停车场的分区维度，为每种车型复制一整套系统会带来无意义的重复状态。
按车型查表就能表达三档费率这条规则，改动小、意图清楚，不需要引入额外的抽象层。
optionExplanations_en: It's just three fixed tiers — there's no case yet where the algorithm needs to be swapped at runtime, so an interface is paying for complexity too early.
Rate is a business policy of the lot; having every ticket carry its own price table means updating each one separately whenever prices change.
Vehicle type isn't a partition of the lot itself, so spinning up a whole separate system per type duplicates state for no reason.
A lookup keyed by vehicle type expresses the three-tier rule directly, with a small change and clear intent, no extra abstraction needed.

scenario: 当前需求只有一条简单的『所有车型同一 hourly rate』定价规则，没有折扣或动态定价。
scenario_en: The current requirement has only one simple pricing rule: the same hourly rate for every vehicle type, with no discounts or dynamic pricing.
q: 为什么基础需求下不一开始就抽 PricingStrategy？
q_en: Why not introduce PricingStrategy at the start for the base requirement?
options: 只有一个简单 hourly rule，提前抽象违反 YAGNI
Strategy pattern 在任何场景下都不好用
Ticket 对象无法传给策略对象
费用计算逻辑不需要写测试
why: 抽象要为真实存在的变化付费；当前只有单一计费规则，直接在 ParkingLot.computeFee 里实现更直接。
why_en: A pricing strategy is premature when the only requirement is one simple hourly rule, which is exactly what YAGNI warns against.
tradeoff: 为当下唯一规则保持直接实现 vs 为假设的未来复杂度提前抽象
options_en: There is only one simple hourly rule, so abstracting early violates YAGNI.
The Strategy pattern is never useful in any scenario.
A Ticket object cannot be passed into a strategy object.
Fee-calculation logic does not need tests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不要为还不存在的需求提前构建抽象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI means you should not build abstraction for a requirement that does not exist yet.

optionExplanations: 目前只有一条统一费率规则，还没有真正的变化要适应，抽出接口只是在为假设的未来付费。
Strategy 模式在规则真的会替换或动态切换时很有用，只是当下这道题还没到那一步。
把 Ticket 传给策略对象在设计上完全可行，这不是不引入 Strategy 的理由。
要不要写测试跟该不该抽象出策略模式是两件不相关的事。
optionExplanations_en: There's only one uniform rate rule right now, with no real variation to accommodate yet, so pulling out an interface pays for a hypothetical future.
The Strategy pattern earns its keep once rules genuinely need to swap or change at runtime — this problem just isn't there yet.
Passing a Ticket into a strategy object is entirely workable in design terms; that isn't the reason to skip Strategy here.
Whether to write tests has nothing to do with whether a strategy pattern is warranted.

scenario: 后续扩展为 10 层商场停车楼。
scenario_en: The design later expands to a ten-floor shopping-mall parking garage.
q: 最自然的新增实体是什么？
q_en: What is the most natural new entity?
options: 把 floorNumber 这个楼层号硬塞进 hourlyRate 计费字段里编码进去
每层建一个独立系统，且不能共享 ticket
ParkingFloor：ParkingLot 持有 floors，Floor 持有 spots
直接删除 ParkingSpot，改用坐标数组
why: ParkingFloor 是 ParkingLot 和 ParkingSpot 之间自然的容器层，spotId 可以顺便携带楼层信息，如 3-A15。
why_en: A multi-floor garage introduces ParkingFloor as a container between ParkingLot and ParkingSpot.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需显示楼层而没有楼层级别的逻辑，也可以把 floorNumber 直接放在 ParkingSpot 上。
tradeoff: 新增中间层容器 vs 把楼层信息硬塞进不相关字段
options_en: Hard-code the floorNumber value by cramming it inside the hourlyRate billing field.
Build an independent system per floor that cannot share tickets.
ParkingFloor: ParkingLot holds floors, and each floor holds spots.
Delete ParkingSpot entirely and use a coordinate array instead.
optionExplanations: 楼层号和费率是两个不相关的字段，把一个编码进另一个会让两者都变得难以理解。
多层楼共享同一批入口和票据体系，拆成互不相通的独立系统会让跨楼层查询无从下手。
在编排者和车位之间加一层容器，正对应现实中的楼层结构，spotId 还能顺便带上楼层号。
坐标数组能表示位置，但丢掉了显式的楼层实体，楼层级别的统计和策略都失去了落脚点。
optionExplanations_en: Floor number and hourly rate are unrelated fields; encoding one inside the other makes both harder to reason about.
A multi-floor garage shares one set of entrances and one ticket system; splitting into isolated per-floor systems breaks any cross-floor query.
Inserting a container layer between the orchestrator and the spots mirrors the physical floor hierarchy directly, and spotId can even carry the floor number along.
A coordinate array can express position, but it drops the explicit floor entity, leaving floor-level stats and policy with nowhere natural to live.

q: 多层扩展后可采用哪些车位分配策略？（多选）
q_en: Which spot-allocation strategies can a multi-floor extension use? (Select all that apply.)
options: 低楼层优先分配
按各层可用车位数量做均衡分配
按目的地或入口距离选择楼层
永远随机选择离入口最远的楼层
why: 不同策略优化不同体验：靠近出口、避免单层拥堵、或靠近目的地；复杂到一定程度可以抽 AllocationStrategy。
why_en: Multi-floor allocation can prioritize lower floors, balance capacity across floors, or optimize for destination proximity.
options_en: Fill lower floors first.
Balance allocation by the number of available spots per floor.
Choose a floor by destination or entrance proximity.
Always randomly pick the floor farthest from the entrance.
optionExplanations: 让车尽量停在离出入口更近的楼层，减少步行距离，是最直接的一种优化目标。
避免某一层被挤爆而其他层空着，均衡分配能把车流压力摊开。
按用户要去的地方选楼层，优化的是从车位到目的地的整体路径，而不只是车位本身。
刻意选最远楼层不服务任何真实目标，只会拉长步行和寻位时间，不是合理策略。
optionExplanations_en: Putting cars on floors closer to the entrance minimizes walking distance — the most direct optimization target.
Balancing spots across floors avoids one floor jamming up while others sit empty, spreading traffic pressure out.
Choosing a floor by where the user is headed optimizes the whole path from spot to destination, not just spot availability.
Deliberately picking the farthest floor serves no real goal — it only lengthens walking and search time, so it isn't a reasonable strategy.

scenario: 多个入口同时调用 enter(CAR)，两个线程都看到同一个 spot 空闲。
scenario_en: Multiple entrances call enter(CAR) at the same time, and two threads both see the same spot as free.
q: 这是哪类问题，最简单的修复方式是什么？
q_en: What kind of problem is this, and what is the simplest fix?
options: 内存泄漏问题；重启服务进程就能解决
check-then-act race；同步整个 enter 关键区
浮点精度误差问题；把金额改成整数 cents
路径解析出错的问题；应该改用 resolvePath 这个工具函数
why: findAvailableSpot 和 occupiedSpotIds.add 必须原子化。同步整个 enter 足够简单，且停车场入场吞吐通常远低于锁能处理的量级。
why_en: Concurrent entries can race between finding and claiming a spot, so the critical section should be synchronized as a whole.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有单一入口，本来就不存在并发，加锁没有必要。
tradeoff: 简单的方法级锁 vs 更细粒度但更复杂的并发方案
options_en: A memory leak; restarting the service process fixes it.
A check-then-act race; synchronize the whole enter critical section.
A floating-point precision bug; switch money to integer cents.
A path-parsing error; the fix should be switching to a resolvePath utility function.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先检查条件再执行动作，中间如果被其他线程插入就会产生竞态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Check-then-act means checking a condition and then acting on it, which races if another thread intervenes in between.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次只能被一个线程执行的代码区域。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A critical section is a block of code that only one thread may execute at a time.

optionExplanations: 内存泄漏是长期占用不释放的问题，两个线程同时看到同一个空位跟内存管理无关。
先检查空闲再写入占用之间有个窗口，两个线程都能钻进去；把查找和占用合成一个临界区能堵住这个窗口。
这里出错的是并发时序，不是数值计算，浮点精度问题不会导致两辆车抢到同一个车位。
场景里没有涉及任何路径或字符串解析逻辑，这个诊断跟症状对不上。
optionExplanations_en: A memory leak is about state never being released over time; two threads seeing the same free spot has nothing to do with memory management.
There's a window between checking free and writing occupied that both threads can slip into; merging the check and the claim into one critical section closes it.
The bug here is concurrency timing, not numeric computation — floating-point precision wouldn't cause two cars to claim the same spot.
Nothing in the scenario involves path or string parsing logic, so this diagnosis doesn't match the symptom.

scenario: 实现多入口并发下的入场分配。
scenario_en: The entry allocation must work correctly when multiple entrances operate concurrently.
q: 这段 synchronized 锁的作用是什么？
q_en: What does this synchronized lock do?
codeSample:
enter(vehicleType)
    synchronized(this)
        spot = findAvailableSpot(vehicleType)
        if spot == null throw NoSpace
        occupiedSpotIds.add(spot.id)
        ticket = Ticket(generateId(), spot.id, vehicleType, now())
        activeTickets[ticket.id] = ticket
        return ticket
options: 只保护 fee 计算这一步
故意设计成让两个入口拿到同一个 spot 才对
替代 ticketId 的生成逻辑
把查找空位、占用和保存 ticket 做成一个原子操作
why: 锁住整个关键区能防止两个线程分配同一车位；这个粒度在停车场规模下通常足够。
why_en: The lock makes spot search, claim, and ticket creation atomic across entrances, preventing two threads from claiming the same spot.
whenOtherWins: 如果持久化到数据库，应改用事务和唯一约束，或 SELECT FOR UPDATE，而不是内存锁。
tradeoff: 粗粒度互斥保证正确 vs 更高并发但更复杂的方案
options_en: It only protects the fee-calculation step.
It is deliberately designed to let two entrances claim the same spot.
It replaces ticket ID generation logic.
It makes spot search, claim, and ticket save one atomic operation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要么完整执行，要么完全不执行，不会被其他线程看到中间状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic operation either completes fully or not at all, with no other thread able to observe a partial result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 互斥锁，同一时刻只允许一个线程进入被保护的代码块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mutex lock allows only one thread at a time to enter the protected section of code.

optionExplanations: 这段代码里没有出现计费逻辑，锁包住的是找位、占位和建票，不是 fee 计算。
加锁的目的正相反，是要阻止两个入口拿到同一个 spot，不是制造这个问题。
generateId() 本来就在锁里被调用，锁不是用来替代它，只是保证它和其他步骤一起原子执行。
锁把找空位、标记占用、创建保存票据这三步合成一个不可分割的操作，别的线程看不到中间状态。
optionExplanations_en: There's no fee-calculation logic in this snippet at all — the lock wraps the search, claim, and ticket steps, not a fee computation.
The whole point of the lock is the opposite — preventing two entrances from claiming the same spot, not causing it.
generateId() is already called inside the lock; the lock isn't replacing it, it's just making it atomic alongside the other steps.
The lock fuses finding a spot, marking it occupied, and creating/storing the ticket into one indivisible operation no other thread can observe mid-way.

scenario: 想让多个入口并发搜索空位，只在真正占用车位时短暂互斥。
scenario_en: We want multiple entrances to search for free spots concurrently and only take a short exclusive lock when claiming a spot.
q: 支持并发搜索、只在占用时短暂独占的更细粒度方案是什么？
q_en: What finer-grained approach supports concurrent search and short exclusive claiming?
options: 读锁搜索，写锁内 double-check 后占用，冲突则重试
完全不加任何锁，读写都自由进行
只锁 activeTickets，不锁 occupiedSpotIds
给每个 ticket 单独分配一把锁
why: 读写锁允许多个搜索并行，但 read 和 write 之间可能被别的线程抢先，所以写锁内要二次检查后再占用。
why_en: A read-write approach searches concurrently, then double-checks and claims the spot under the write lock, retrying on conflict.
whenOtherWins: 对 3-5 个入口的普通停车场，方法级互斥更简单，性能也已经足够。
tradeoff: 读写锁提高并发但要 double-check vs 单一互斥锁简单但完全串行
options_en: Search under a read lock, then double-check and claim under a write lock, retrying on conflict.
Use no locking at all for reads or writes.
Lock only activeTickets and leave occupiedSpotIds unlocked.
Give every ticket its own separate lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许多个读操作并发进行，但写操作需要独占访问的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read-write lock lets multiple readers run concurrently but gives a writer exclusive access.

optionExplanations: 读多写少的场景下，多个搜索可以并发跑，真正占用车位那一刻才切到写锁并二次确认，兼顾并发度和正确性。
不加锁能获得最大并发，但代价是彻底放弃正确性，check-then-act 的窗口会天天暴露。
占用状态实际记在 occupiedSpotIds 里，只锁 activeTickets 完全保护不到真正会冲突的数据。
冲突发生在多个线程抢同一个 spot，而不是抢同一张 ticket，按 ticket 分锁根本锁不住这场竞争。
optionExplanations_en: When reads dominate, multiple searches can run concurrently and only the moment of claiming switches to a write lock with a re-check, balancing concurrency against correctness.
No locking at all buys maximum concurrency, but at the cost of correctness entirely — the check-then-act window gets exposed every time.
Occupancy actually lives in occupiedSpotIds; locking only activeTickets doesn't protect the data that can actually conflict.
The conflict is multiple threads racing for the same spot, not the same ticket, so a per-ticket lock doesn't guard against that race at all.

q: 按顺序排列多入口 race 的发生过程：
q_en: Put the multi-entrance race in order:
steps: 入口 A 和 B 同时调用 findAvailableSpot。
二者都看到 spot B 不在 occupiedSpotIds 里。
A 创建 ticket 指向 spot B。
B 也创建 ticket 指向 spot B。
两辆车拿到了同一个车位。
why: 问题窗口在『检查空闲』和『写入占用』之间；必须把两步合并成同一个临界区才能消除这个 race。
why_en: The race occurs because two entrances observe the same free spot before either one claims it, so the check and the claim must become one critical section.
tradeoff: 分离的检查与占用步骤 vs 合并成一个原子临界区
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Gate A
  participant S as spot B
  participant B as Gate B
  A->>S: sees free
  B->>S: sees free
  A->>S: claim
  B->>S: claim

termDefinitions.meaning: 多线程同时读写共享状态导致结果依赖执行顺序的错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition happens when concurrent threads read and write shared state and the outcome depends on timing.

scenario: 停车场有 3-5 个入口，单次 enter 处理约 100 毫秒；200 个车位平均每 2 小时周转一次。
scenario_en: The lot has 3 to 5 entrances, one enter call takes about 100 ms, and 200 spots turn over about once every 2 hours on average.
q: 为什么同步整个 enter() 方法在现实停车场规模下通常足够？
q_en: Why is synchronizing the whole enter() method usually enough at real parking-lot scale?
options: 因为加锁本身会让车位的物理数量凭空增加
因为这类题目里假设停车场永远只有一个车位
因为 ticket map 的按 ID 查找本身非常慢
入场频率远低于锁可处理的吞吐，车通过闸机/支付耗时远大于内存操作
why: 工程取舍要看数量级：停车场的真实入场频率很低，简单正确的方案应该优先于过早优化。
why_en: A coarse enter lock is usually fine because parking-lot arrival rates are tiny compared with in-memory critical-section throughput.
tradeoff: 按数量级判断是否需要优化 vs 不看数量级就上复杂并发方案
options_en: Because locking itself somehow makes the physical spot count grow.
Because this kind of problem always assumes only one spot exists.
Because ticket-map lookup by ID is itself extremely slow.
Arrival frequency is far below what the lock can handle, since gate and payment time dwarf in-memory work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间内系统能处理的请求数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throughput is the number of requests a system can process per unit of time.

optionExplanations: 加锁只是控制并发访问顺序，不会改变车位这类物理资源的数量，这个因果关系不成立。
题目场景是 200 个车位、3-5 个入口，不是只有一个车位的极端情况。
map 查找是微秒级操作，慢的从来不是查找本身。
锁能处理的吞吐是微秒到毫秒级，而真实入场受限于闸机和支付这些慢得多的物理环节，锁根本不是瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Locking only controls the order of concurrent access; it can't change how many physical spots exist — that causal link doesn't hold.
The scenario is 200 spots and 3-5 entrances, not the degenerate case of a single spot.
Map lookup runs in microseconds — lookup speed was never the slow part here.
The lock can handle throughput on the order of microseconds to milliseconds, while real entries are bottlenecked by gates and payment, which are far slower — the lock is never the constraint.

scenario: 有人说 Node.js 单线程就完全不会有 race condition。
scenario_en: Someone claims Node.js is single-threaded, so race conditions cannot happen at all.
q: 面对这个说法应该如何回应？
q_en: How should you respond to that claim?
options: 单线程模型下永远不会出现逻辑上的 race
异步 await 之间仍可能交错，持久化时要靠数据库事务或分布式锁保证原子性
Node.js 这门编程语言本身就完全不适合拿来实现这样的停车场系统
只要用 Set 存状态就自动获得事务保证
why: 单线程事件循环避免了同一时刻执行两段 JS，但异步 I/O 会在 await 点把请求流程切开，数据库层仍要保证 check-and-claim 原子。
why_en: Single-threaded event loops can still interleave async workflows at await points, so persistence still needs transactional protection.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有状态更新都在同一个不跨越 await 的同步代码块里，才真的不需要额外加锁。
tradeoff: 单线程避免同一时刻双执行 vs 异步交错仍需事务或分布式锁
options_en: A single-threaded model can never have a logical race.
Async await points can still interleave, so persistence needs database transactions or a distributed lock.
Node.js as a programming language is simply never suited at all for building a system like this parking lot.
Storing state in a Set automatically gives you transaction guarantees.

termDefinitions.meaning: Node.js 单线程调度模型，在 I/O 等待点切换执行其他任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The event loop is Node.js's single-threaded scheduler that switches to other work while one task waits on I/O.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨多个进程或服务器协调、只允许一个持有者继续执行的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock coordinates across multiple processes or servers so only one holder can proceed at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库锁定被查询的行，防止其他事务并发修改它们。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT FOR UPDATE locks the selected database rows so no other transaction can modify them concurrently.

optionExplanations: 单线程只保证同一时刻只有一段 JS 在跑，但 await 会把一次操作拆成好几段，中间照样能被别的请求插进来。
两个 await 之间事件循环会去处理别的任务，状态要落库时还是得靠数据库事务或分布式锁保证检查和占用是一体的。
语言的并发模型只影响要不要额外加锁，跟这门语言适不适合实现某个系统是两件事。
Set 只是一种数据结构，本身不提供任何跨请求的原子性或回滚能力。
optionExplanations_en: Single-threaded only guarantees one piece of JS runs at a time — await splits one operation into several steps, and another request can still slip in between them.
Between two await points the event loop can go handle other work, so if state is persisted, it still needs a database transaction or distributed lock to keep check-and-claim atomic.
The language's concurrency model only affects whether extra locking is needed — that's a separate question from whether it's suited to building the system at all.
A Set is just a data structure; it provides no cross-request atomicity or rollback on its own.

scenario: ticketId 从未存在过，或者已经出场使用过一次。
scenario_en: The ticketId either never existed or was already used once at exit.
q: 基础 exit 应该对这两种情况返回什么语义？
q_en: What semantic result should base exit return for these two cases?
options: 必须区分成两个不同的复杂错误码
自动为用户重新发一张新 ticket
两种情况统一视为 invalid ticket
照常释放一个任意车位再报错
why: activeTickets 只表示当前有效票据集合，不存在和已使用对出场流程都是不可用，没必要区分。
why_en: A ticket not present in activeTickets is invalid whether it never existed or was already used, so exit treats them the same.
whenOtherWins: 如果客服或审计需要区分这两种情况，可以额外保存历史 used tickets 和状态。
tradeoff: 统一 invalid 语义换实现简单 vs 区分两种错误换更精确反馈
options_en: The two cases must be distinguished with two different complex error codes.
Automatically issue the user a brand-new ticket.
Treat both cases uniformly as an invalid ticket.
Free some arbitrary spot anyway before reporting an error.
optionExplanations: 两种情况对出场流程的结果都一样——都不能继续，区分成两个错误码是给基础流程增加不必要的分支。
无效票据不该被系统当成新会话来处理，自动补发一张票会掩盖真正的问题。
系统只用『当前有效』这一个状态描述票据，不在这个集合里的票据不管原因是什么，对出场来说都是同一种结果。
错误的票据本来就没有对应的正确车位，随便释放一个反而会破坏别的会话的占用状态。
optionExplanations_en: Both cases lead to the same outcome for exit — neither can proceed — so splitting them into two error codes adds branching the base flow doesn't need.
An invalid ticket shouldn't be treated as the start of a new session; auto-issuing a replacement would paper over the real problem.
The system expresses only one state, currently valid; anything missing from that set produces the same result for exit, regardless of why.
An invalid ticket has no spot it actually corresponds to, so releasing some arbitrary one would corrupt another session's occupancy instead.

scenario: 后续要支持车位维修或临时封闭。
scenario_en: A later requirement adds spot maintenance or temporary closure.
q: 在当前占用建模（occupiedSpotIds Set）下，新增维修状态最自然放在哪里？
q_en: With the current occupiedSpotIds Set model, where should maintenance state go?
options: ParkingSpot 加 status 字段，或 ParkingLot 加 disabledSpotIds 过滤
在 Ticket 记录上增加一个记录维修人员姓名和联系方式的字段
往 VehicleType 这个车辆分类 enum 类型里硬是新增一个 BROKEN 取值来表示这个新状态
把这个车位的 hourlyRate 计费字段直接改成 0 表示不可用
why: 维修是车位自身或可用性约束，不是 ticket 会话的一部分；基础设计没有实现，但可以沿分配过滤自然扩展。
why_en: Maintenance can be modeled as spot status or a disabled-spot-ID set that allocation simply skips.
whenOtherWins: 如果车位物理状态很多，ParkingSpot.status enum 更适合；只是临时屏蔽少数车位，用 disabled set 更轻量。
tradeoff: 维护性状态放进车位可用性过滤 vs 混进车辆分类或计价字段
options_en: Add a status field to ParkingSpot, or a disabledSpotIds filter on ParkingLot.
Add a field on the Ticket record storing the maintenance worker's name and contact info.
Hard-add a brand-new BROKEN value into the VehicleType vehicle-classification enum type just to represent this new state.
Change that spot's hourlyRate billing field directly to zero to mark it unusable.
optionExplanations: 维修状态描述的是车位本身能不能用，跟 ParkingSpot 的固有属性天然是一类，扩展起来最顺。
Ticket 描述的是一次停车会话，跟车位要不要维修是完全不相关的两条线。
VehicleType 分类的是车辆而不是车位，BROKEN 描述的是车位状态，塞进这个 enum 混淆了两个维度。
费率是计价字段，把它改成 0 只是掩盖了『不可用』这件事，还会让计费逻辑读到假价格。
optionExplanations_en: Maintenance status describes whether the spot itself can be used, which naturally belongs alongside ParkingSpot's own properties — the easiest place to extend.
Ticket describes one parking session; whether a spot needs maintenance is an entirely unrelated concern.
VehicleType classifies vehicles, not spots — BROKEN describes spot state, so cramming it into that enum conflates two different dimensions.
Rate is a pricing field; zeroing it out only hides the 'unavailable' fact and leaves fee logic reading a fake price.

scenario: 监控或前端目前都没有提出『查询实时车位状态』的需求。
scenario_en: Neither monitoring nor the frontend currently requires querying real-time spot status.
q: 为什么基础 API 不主动加 getAvailableSpots 或 getParkingStatus？
q_en: Why should the base API not proactively add getAvailableSpots or getParkingStatus?
options: 这两个方法在技术上根本无法实现
需求没有要求，暴露内部状态会扩大 API；监控需求来了再加
加了这两个方法会破坏 ticketId 的唯一性
使用者必须提前知道全部车位信息
why: 接口应该围绕核心工作流最小化；过早暴露内部集合会增加耦合，等真正的监控需求出现再加不迟。
why_en: The base API stays focused on entry and exit until status queries are explicitly required, to avoid premature coupling.
tradeoff: 接口按需最小化 vs 提前暴露内部状态换『可能有用』
options_en: These two methods are technically impossible to implement.
There is no requirement for them, and exposing internal state widens the API; add them when monitoring is actually needed.
Adding them would break the uniqueness of ticketId.
Callers must already know the full spot inventory in advance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只暴露必要的公开接口，隐藏内部实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means exposing only the necessary public interface while hiding internal implementation details.

optionExplanations: 查询车位状态在技术上没有任何障碍，说做不到是站不住脚的。
没有监控或前端提出这个需求，先加上等于提前把内部索引暴露成公开接口，真需要时再加不迟。
这两个方法是只读查询，跟 ticketId 怎么生成、是否唯一完全没有关系。
现在的入场出场流程不要求调用方提前知道任何车位库存信息。
optionExplanations_en: There's no technical obstacle to querying spot status; claiming it's impossible doesn't hold up.
Neither monitoring nor the frontend has asked for this yet, so adding it now means turning an internal index into a public API early — it can be added the moment it's actually needed.
These are read-only queries and have nothing to do with how ticketId is generated or whether it stays unique.
The current entry/exit flow doesn't require a caller to know anything about spot inventory ahead of time.

q: 出场计费的正确执行顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct order for exit fee calculation?
steps: 从 activeTickets 取出 ticket。
计算 exitTime - entryTime。
按小时向上取整。
乘以 hourlyRateCents。
释放 spot 并删除 ticket。
why: 必须先有 ticket 才能知道 entryTime 和 spotId；删除 ticket 前要先取够计费和释放所需的数据。
why_en: Exit fee calculation uses the active ticket's entry time, rounds duration up, multiplies by the rate, and only then clears state.
tradeoff: 先读后清理保证数据完整 vs 先清理导致计费数据丢失

scenario: 所有 car spotId 都已经在 occupiedSpotIds 中，此时来了一辆车，车辆类型为 CAR。
scenario_en: All car spot IDs are already in occupiedSpotIds, and now a CAR arrives.
q: enter(CAR) 应该如何处理？
q_en: How should enter(CAR) behave?
options: 发一张 ticket，但 spotId 留空
拒绝入场，且不创建 ticket
临时占用一个 motorcycle spot
把最早入场的旧 ticket 强制删除
why: 没有兼容空位时不能创建停车会话；创建一张没有 spot 的 ticket 会破坏 exit 释放逻辑的不变量。
why_en: Entry must fail without creating a ticket when no compatible spot is available.
whenOtherWins: 如果支持候补排队，可以创建一个 WaitingRequest，但那不是基础 ticket 流程。
tradeoff: 无空位时拒绝并保持状态不变 vs 创建残缺 ticket 破坏不变量
options_en: Issue a ticket but leave spotId empty.
Reject entry and create no ticket at all.
Temporarily occupy a motorcycle spot instead.
Force-remove the oldest active ticket to make room.
optionExplanations: spotId 留空的票据后面没法出场释放车位，等于制造了一条无法闭环的记录。
没有兼容空位时最直接的做法就是不创建任何状态、直接拒绝，保持系统状态一致。
car 不兼容 motorcycle spot，临时借用会破坏『按车型精确匹配』这条基础规则。
强制清退别人正在使用的合法车位，本质上是抢别人的车位来解决自己的容量问题。
optionExplanations_en: A ticket with an empty spotId has no spot to release at exit later — it creates a record that can never close cleanly.
With no compatible spot available, the most direct move is to create no state at all and simply reject, keeping the system consistent.
A car isn't compatible with a motorcycle spot; borrowing one anyway breaks the exact-type-match rule the base design relies on.
Force-evicting someone else's legitimate, still-active session is really just stealing their spot to solve your own capacity problem.

scenario: 多层停车楼希望根据不同目标（靠近出口/均衡/靠近目的地）选择不同分配策略。
scenario_en: A multi-floor garage wants to switch allocation policies based on goals such as nearest exit, load balancing, or destination proximity.
q: 何时应该引入 AllocationStrategy？
q_en: When should AllocationStrategy be introduced?
options: 单层 exact-match 场景一开始就必须引入
当 Ticket 没有 entryTime 字段时
当金额改用 cents 存储时
当分配规则会在低楼层优先、均衡、目的地接近等策略间切换时
why: Strategy 模式适合真实存在、可能被替换的算法；基础单一规则下直接实现更简洁。
why_en: AllocationStrategy earns its complexity when spot-selection policy genuinely varies and needs to be swapped.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有单层、单一规则，不必引入 Strategy，直接 inline 实现更清楚。
tradeoff: 真实可替换算法才上 Strategy vs 单一规则直接内联实现
options_en: The single-floor exact-match case must introduce it right away.
When the Ticket has no entryTime field.
When money switches to storing cents.
When allocation policy genuinely switches among lowest-floor-first, balanced, and destination-proximity strategies.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["one simple allocation rule"] --> B["inline method"]
  C["multiple changing policies"] --> D["AllocationStrategy"]
  D --> E["nearest, cheapest, level aware"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可替换的算法封装成独立类，运行时可以互换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Strategy pattern encapsulates interchangeable algorithms as separate classes that can be swapped at runtime.

optionExplanations: 只有一条精确匹配规则时还没有『多种算法互换』这个需求，一开始就上 Strategy 是提前抽象。
entryTime 缺不缺跟怎么选车位是两回事，这个条件跟分配策略没有因果关系。
金额存储方式是计费问题，跟车位该怎么分配是完全不相关的两条逻辑。
当低楼层优先、均衡、目的地接近这些规则会互相替换或组合时，『可插拔算法』的需求才真正出现，Strategy 才值回复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: With only one exact-match rule, there's no 'swap between algorithms' need yet — introducing Strategy at the start is abstracting too early.
Whether entryTime exists is unrelated to how a spot gets chosen; that condition has no causal link to allocation policy.
How money is stored is a billing concern, entirely separate from the logic of choosing a spot.
Once rules like lowest-floor-first, balanced, and destination-proximity actually need to swap or combine, a genuine 'pluggable algorithm' need shows up — that's when Strategy earns its complexity.

q: 补全三类对象的职责：
q_en: Fill in the responsibilities of the three object types:
text: ParkingLot 管 {{分配、activeTickets、occupiedSpotIds、计费}}；ParkingSpot 管 {{id 和 spotType}}；Ticket 管 {{ticketId、spotId、vehicleType、entryTime}}。
why: 职责边界清晰后，入场和出场流程都变成 orchestrator 对简单记录和物理资源的协调。
why_en: ParkingLot owns workflows and indexes, ParkingSpot owns intrinsic spot properties, and Ticket records a session.

q: Senior 级 Parking Lot 回答应主动覆盖哪些技术要点？（多选）
q_en: Which technical points should a senior-level Parking Lot answer cover proactively? (Select all that apply.)
options: Vehicle 不建实体的理由
occupied flag / derived / Set 三种方案的权衡
Ticket 用 map 按 ID 查找的理由
金额用整数 cents 存储
多入口并发 race 的成因和加锁方案
why: 高级答案要能主动解释状态归属、数据结构选择和并发正确性，而不仅仅是列出类图。
why_en: Senior answers explain entity pruning, occupancy tradeoffs, ticket lookup, integer money, and multi-entrance races without being prompted.
options_en: Why Vehicle is not modeled as an entity.
The tradeoffs among flag, derived, and Set approaches to occupancy.
Why Ticket lookup uses a map keyed by ID.
Storing money as integer cents.
The cause of multi-entrance races and how to lock against them.
optionExplanations: 能主动说清车辆为什么只是分类标签而不是实体，说明理解状态归属这条主线。
能对比三种占用方案的查找成本和加锁边界，说明不是死记答案，而是懂权衡。
能说出用 map 而不是 list 的原因，展示的是对数据结构选择背后意图的理解。
主动提到用整数分存钱，说明对精度这类容易被单独追问的细节有防备。
能主动指出多入口下的 race 窗口并给出加锁方案，是这道题体现并发意识的关键得分点。
optionExplanations_en: Being able to explain unprompted why Vehicle stays a label instead of an entity shows the candidate follows the state-modeling thread.
Comparing lookup cost and locking boundaries across the three occupancy approaches shows real tradeoff understanding, not a memorized answer.
Explaining why a map beats a list demonstrates understanding of the intent behind a data-structure choice, not just the choice itself.
Volunteering integer-cent storage shows the candidate is ahead of a precision question the interviewer might otherwise probe separately.
Proactively naming the multi-entrance race window and its fix is the key signal of concurrency awareness in this problem.

q: 按顺序排列 Parking Lot 的主设计链路：
q_en: Put the main Parking Lot design argument in order:
steps: ParkingLot 作为入口，持有 spots、occupiedSpotIds、activeTickets、hourlyRateCents。
澄清三类车、自动兼容分配、ticket、出场计费和释放。
Vehicle 降级为 enum，Ticket 建成不可变会话记录。
占用建模为 ParkingLot 维护的关系索引 Set。
enter/exit 分别原子维护 ticket 和 occupied spot 状态。
why: 从范围澄清到实体裁剪，再到状态归属和流程不变量，是这道题的主要论证路径。
why_en: The design chain moves from scoped requirements to entity pruning, orchestrator state, occupancy indexing, and lifecycle updates.
tradeoff: 范围裁剪先行再定状态归属 vs 一上来就画类图

scenario: 系统需要同时用 occupiedSpotIds 和 activeTickets 两个索引描述同一次停车会话，两者必须保持同步。
scenario_en: The system uses both occupiedSpotIds and activeTickets to describe the same parking session, and the two indexes must stay in sync.
q: 面试收尾时，哪一句最准确地总结这个不变量？
q_en: Which closing sentence best summarizes this invariant in an interview?
options: 系统里每一辆曾经进出过的车辆，不管现在是否已经离开车场了，都必须始终对应一个持久化保存完整状态的 Vehicle 实体类
active ticket 指向的 spotId 必须在 occupiedSpotIds 中；成功 exit 后二者都要被删除
所有车位的编号命名必须在整个停车场范围内按楼层严格连续排序
所有发出的 ticket 只要生成成功就永久有效，理论上永远不会失效或过期
why: ParkingLot 用两个索引表达同一会话；入场同时创建两者，出场同时清理两者，才能避免重复出场或重复分配。
why_en: The key invariant is that active tickets and occupied spot IDs stay in sync for every parking session.
whenOtherWins: 如果从 activeTickets 推导 occupancy，就不需要维护 Set，但分配时要保护对 tickets 的读取和修改。
tradeoff: 双索引同步的不变量 vs 单一来源但需要每次重新推导
options_en: Every single vehicle that has ever entered, whether or not it has already left the lot by now, must always have a persisted, fully stateful Vehicle entity class.
The spotId an active ticket points to must be in occupiedSpotIds, and a successful exit removes both.
Spot numbers must be strictly and continuously sorted by floor across the entire lot.
Every issued ticket stays valid forever once created, theoretically never expiring or timing out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在任何时刻都必须保持成立的约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a condition the system must always keep true.

optionExplanations: 车辆从头到尾都只是分类标签，这句总结把它错误地升级成了需要持久化的实体。
两个索引描述同一件事，出场那一刻必须同时清理，这才是真正撑住系统的不变量。
车位编号怎么命名是展示细节，不是这道题真正要保护的正确性约束。
如果票据永远有效，重复出场和重复释放的风险就无法被排除，这跟不变量的方向正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: A vehicle was only ever a classification label; this statement wrongly promotes it to something requiring persisted entity state.
Both indexes describe the same fact and must always agree, with exit clearing both at the same moment — that's what actually holds the system together.
How spot numbers are labeled is a display detail, not the correctness constraint this problem is protecting.
If a ticket stayed valid forever, double-exit and double-release risk could never be ruled out — the opposite of what the invariant guarantees.

scenario: 面试官按中级候选人的标准评估这道 Parking Lot 设计。
scenario_en: The interviewer evaluates this Parking Lot design at the mid-level candidate bar.
q: 中级候选人在本题应能稳定说明什么？
q_en: What should a mid-level candidate be able to explain reliably in this problem?
options: 必须一次性实现多层楼分配策略并处理跨楼层并发锁
无论如何都必须使用数据库事务加上 SELECT FOR UPDATE 语句来保证强一致性
必须把 Vehicle 建成完整类并存车主、车牌信息
ParkingLot 编排、ParkingSpot 存属性、Ticket 是记录，能处理三类边界情况
why: 中级重点是职责清晰和关键边界情况；多层策略和并发多入口是高级候选人再深入的部分。
why_en: A mid-level answer should clearly separate ParkingLot, ParkingSpot, and Ticket and handle the key entry and exit edge cases.
tradeoff: 中级看职责分离与边界情况 vs 高级才要求的并发/多层深挖
options_en: Implement multi-floor allocation and cross-floor concurrency locking in one pass.
Database transactions plus a SELECT FOR UPDATE statement must always be used no matter what, to guarantee strong consistency.
Build Vehicle as a full class storing owner and license-plate information.
ParkingLot orchestrates, ParkingSpot stores properties, Ticket is a record, and it handles the three key edge cases.
optionExplanations: 多层分配和跨楼层并发是这道题深挖之后才出现的加分项，不是中级候选人一次要做完的基线。
题目场景是内存态设计，数据库事务是持久化层的加分项，不是中级候选人的硬性门槛。
把 Vehicle 建成完整类恰好是这道题要避免的过度设计，中级候选人应反过来说明为什么不这么做。
分清谁编排、谁存属性、谁是记录，再处理满位、无效票据、重复出场三类边界情况，是中级候选人真正的及格线。
optionExplanations_en: Multi-floor allocation and cross-floor concurrency only show up once the problem gets pushed deeper — they aren't the mid-level baseline for a single pass.
This scenario is an in-memory design; database transactions are a persistence-layer bonus, not a hard bar for a mid-level candidate.
Building Vehicle as a full class is exactly the over-engineering this problem wants avoided — a mid-level candidate should explain why not, if anything.
Separating who orchestrates, who stores properties, and who is a record, plus handling the full-lot, invalid-ticket, and double-exit edge cases, is the actual mid-level bar here.

scenario: entryTime 和 exitTime 相同，车辆几乎立刻出场。
scenario_en: entryTime and exitTime are the same because the vehicle exits almost immediately.
q: 按『hourly rounded up』规则，durationMillis 为 0 时应如何思考？
q_en: Under an hourly-rounded-up rule, how should you reason about durationMillis = 0?
options: 永远都应该直接收取 0，完全不追问产品是否需要设定最低消费门槛
永远收 24 小时，把这种情况当成整天处理
是否收 0 或 1 小时要先向产品澄清；非零但不足一小时仍向上收 1 小时
认为这种边界情况在数学上根本无法算出费用
why: 计费规则强调部分小时向上取整，但 0 分钟是否有最低收费属于产品语义，面试中应该主动澄清或明确定义，而不是自己假设。
why_en: Partial hours clearly round up, but the exact zero-duration minimum charge is a product rule that should be clarified rather than assumed.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务明确规定最低一小时收费，那么 duration 为 0 时也直接返回一小时的费用。
tradeoff: 边界语义需要产品澄清 vs 默认套用向上取整规则
options_en: It should always just charge exactly 0 outright every time, without ever asking product whether a minimum charge applies.
Always charge 24 hours, treating this edge case as a full day.
Clarify with product whether 0 or 1 hour applies; any nonzero partial hour still rounds up to 1.
Claim this edge case is mathematically impossible to bill at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无论实际使用多短，至少收取的费用下限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A minimum charge is the smallest fee charged regardless of how briefly the resource was used.

optionExplanations: 直接收 0 是自己替产品做了『不设最低消费』的决定，边界语义没有被真正澄清。
把瞬间出场当成整天收费缺乏依据，跟计费规则里『向上取整到小时』的粒度完全对不上。
取整规则本身很清楚，但零时长要不要收最低一小时是产品语义，主动提出澄清比自己瞎猜更稳妥。
取模加乘法就能算出 0，这个边界情况在数学上没有任何障碍。
optionExplanations_en: Charging 0 outright silently decides on the product's behalf that there's no minimum charge — the edge case was never actually clarified.
Billing a full day for an instant exit has no basis; it doesn't match the hourly rounding granularity the rule actually describes.
The rounding rule itself is clear, but whether zero duration still hits a one-hour minimum is a product decision — raising it beats guessing.
Modulo plus multiplication computes 0 without issue; there's no mathematical obstacle in this edge case at all.
